Shephatiah
shef-a-tī'ä
n. (the head of a family of three hundred seventy and two who returned from the captivity; also a son of David, and one of the princes who cast Jeremiah into the dungeon)
From Hebrew Shephatyah, the LORD hath judged, from shaphat, to judge or vindicate, with Yah. The verb is the one behind shophet, a judge, and behind the title of the book of Judges.

Biblical Definition

Shephatiah heads one of the families counted twice in the register of the return, with the same figure both times: “The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy and two” (Ezr 2:4), and again “The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy and two” (Neh 7:9). A second contingent of the house came up later with Ezra: “And of the sons of Shephatiah; Zebadiah the son of Michael, and with him fourscore males” (Ezr 8:8). The name is borne by better and worse men. One Shephatiah was the fifth son born to David in Hebron (2Sa 3:4). Another was a son of Jehoshaphat, killed with his brothers by Jehoram (2Ch 21:2-4). And one is among the four princes who heard Jeremiah preaching surrender and demanded his death: “Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people” (Jer 38:1), and it was on their motion that the prophet was let down into the miry dungeon of Malchiah. The name means the LORD hath judged, and one man who bore it was in the room when a nation refused the word of the LORD's judgment and threw the messenger into a pit.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) has no article for Shephatiah; in sacred history it is the name of a family of the return, of a son of David, and of a prince in the days of Jeremiah.

SHEPHATIAH, n. The LORD hath judged; a proper name borne by several men.

The head of a family, three hundred seventy and two of whose children returned with Zerubbabel.

Fourscore males of the same house came up afterward with Ezra.

The fifth son born to David in Hebron was named Shephatiah.

A prince of that name was among those who cast Jeremiah into the dungeon.

Modern Corruption

There is no significant modern redefinition of this name. The principle to recover is that the register of the returned is a real census of real households, and that God preserves His church by families and by name.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Shephatiah is a family head in a census and nobody has contested him. What the register sets against a modern reader who skims it is the character of God's preservation of His people. The list is not round. Three hundred seventy and two, ninety and eight, two thousand fifty and six, an hundred thirty and nine — awkward numbers, counted twice, seventy years apart, and agreeing. Somebody kept those books through the captivity, and the Holy Ghost saw fit to put them in the canon.

The principle to recover is that the church is not an abstraction but a named people. The Lord “calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out” (Joh 10:3); the book of life has names written in it; Paul ends his epistles with rolls of greetings that no editor would have invented. A congregation that keeps no membership roll, knows no households, and cannot say who belongs to it has drifted from the pattern of a book that troubled to record that the children of Shephatiah were three hundred seventy and two.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Shephatyah (H8203), the LORD hath judged; shaphat (H8199), to judge, vindicate; Yah (H3050), the LORD; miphqad — see yachas (H3187), to reckon by genealogy; bor (H953), pit, dungeon.

expand to see more

Hebrew Shephatyah (H8203) — Shephatiah; the LORD hath judged.

Hebrew shaphat (H8199) — to judge; the root of the name.

Hebrew Yah (H3050) — the LORD; the divine element.

Hebrew yachas (H3187) — to reckon by genealogy; the work of the registers.

Hebrew bor (H953) — pit; the dungeon Jeremiah was let down into.

Usage

"“The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy and two” — a family counted twice and agreeing."

"“And with him fourscore males” — a second company of the same house."

"“Shephatiah the son of Mattan” — the name on a worse errand."
